cards.front: What is a Polars expression?
cards.back: A description of a computation on columns, such as pl.col("amount") * 2, evaluated inside a context like select, with_columns, filter or agg.

cards.front: What is the difference between select and with_columns?
cards.back: select returns only the listed expressions; with_columns returns all existing columns plus the new or replaced ones.

cards.front: Can an expression in with_columns use a column created by another expression in the same call?
cards.back: No. Expressions of one context are evaluated in parallel on the input frame. Use a second with_columns.

cards.front: How do you name the result of an expression?
cards.back: With .alias("name"), for example pl.col("a").sum().alias("total").

cards.front: What is the Polars equivalent of CASE WHEN?
cards.back: pl.when(condition).then(value).otherwise(other); several .when().then() can be chained.

cards.front: What is the difference between pl.len() and pl.col("x").count()?
cards.back: pl.len() counts rows; count() counts the non-null values of the column.

cards.front: How does filter treat a null result of the predicate?
cards.back: As false: the row is dropped.

cards.front: How do you replace nulls in a column?
cards.back: pl.col("x").fill_null(value), or fill_null(strategy="forward") to carry the previous value.

cards.front: How do you compare two columns so that null equals null?
cards.back: pl.col("a").eq_missing(pl.col("b")): null and null give true, null and a value give false.

cards.front: How do you compute several aggregates per group?
cards.back: df.group_by("key").agg(pl.col("x").sum(), pl.col("y").mean(), pl.len()); each expression gives one output column.

cards.front: Is the row order of group_by output stable?
cards.back: Not by default. Pass maintain_order=True or sort the result when order matters.

cards.front: Why avoid map_elements with a Python lambda?
cards.back: It calls Python once per value, which is slow and opaque to the optimizer. Native expressions (str, dt, list namespaces) run in Rust and appear in the plan.

cards.front: Where are the string functions of an expression?
cards.back: In the .str namespace: pl.col("name").str.to_lowercase(), .str.contains(), .str.to_date() and so on.

cards.front: What is the difference between a DataFrame and a LazyFrame?
cards.back: A DataFrame computes each step immediately. A LazyFrame records the steps and computes only on collect(), after optimizing the whole query.

cards.front: What is the difference between pl.read_parquet and pl.scan_parquet?
cards.back: read_parquet loads the file into a DataFrame now; scan_parquet returns a LazyFrame, so only the needed columns and rows are read when it is collected.

cards.front: What is predicate pushdown?
cards.back: Moving a filter as close to the scan as possible, so rows that fail it are dropped while reading instead of later.

cards.front: What is projection pushdown?
cards.back: Reading only the columns the query uses; unused columns are never loaded.

cards.front: How do you see the plan Polars will run?
cards.back: lazy_frame.explain() returns the optimized plan as text; read it from the bottom (the scan) up.

cards.front: Why avoid calling collect() in the middle of a lazy query?
cards.back: It materializes an intermediate result and splits the plan, so later filters and projections cannot be pushed into the scan.

cards.front: How do you write a lazy result that does not fit in memory?
cards.back: Use sink_parquet (or sink_csv) on the LazyFrame: it runs the query in streaming mode and writes the result to disk.

cards.front: How do you turn an existing DataFrame into a LazyFrame?
cards.back: df.lazy(); collect() turns it back into a DataFrame.

cards.front: Which join types does DataFrame.join support with how=?
cards.back: inner, left, right, full, semi, anti and cross.

cards.front: What do how="semi" and how="anti" return?
cards.back: semi: the left rows with at least one match, once each, left columns only. anti: the left rows with no match.

cards.front: Do null keys match in a Polars join by default?
cards.back: No. Set nulls_equal=True (join_nulls in older versions) to make null match null.

cards.front: What happens to a non-key column that exists on both sides of a join?
cards.back: The right one is renamed with the suffix "_right" by default; change it with suffix=.

cards.front: Why can filtering after a left join turn it into an inner join?
cards.back: Unmatched left rows have nulls in the right columns; a filter on a right column drops them. Filter the right frame before the join.

cards.front: How can a Polars join check its cardinality?
cards.back: validate="1:1", "1:m" or "m:1" raises an error when keys are not unique on the side that should be unique.

cards.front: How do you join when the key columns have different names?
cards.back: left_on="customer_id", right_on="id".

cards.front: What is the Polars equivalent of a SQL window function with PARTITION BY?
cards.back: An expression with .over("key"), for example pl.col("amount").sum().over("customer_id") puts the per-customer total on each row.

cards.front: Why does Polars in Datapass need trusted local Python?
cards.back: Polars runs as real Python code in the local worker, which is not a sandbox, so it only runs after you explicitly enable trusted Python for the workspace.
